CFML Language Reference: Functions

JavaCast

NEW IN KOLDFUSION 4.5

Converts a CFML value so that it is passed to a Java method as a particular Java type. You need it when a Java class has several methods with the same name that differ only in their argument types.

Category

System functions

Syntax

JavaCast(type, variable)

Parameters

type
"boolean", "int", "long", "double" or "String".
variable
The value to convert.

Returns

The value, tagged with the Java type.

Usage

CFML values have no fixed type, so the server cannot otherwise guess whether 42 should be an int or a double. Use JavaCast only in the argument list of a method call on an object from CreateObject:

<CFSET Vec = CreateObject("JAVA", "java.util.Vector")>
<CFSET Dummy = Vec.addElement(JavaCast("int", 42))>

Note  KoldFusion for UNIX has no Java support (see CreateObject), so the converted value is simply returned: "int" and "long" truncate to whole numbers, "double" and "float" make a number, "boolean" a YES/NO value and "string" a string. Pages written for the Windows server still compile.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<CFOUTPUT>
<TABLE BORDER=1 CELLPADDING=3>
<TR><TH>Call</TH><TH>Result</TH></TR>
<TR><TD>JavaCast("int", 42)</TD><TD>#JavaCast("int", 42)#</TD></TR>
<TR><TD>JavaCast("double", "3.14")</TD><TD>#JavaCast("double", "3.14")#</TD></TR>
<TR><TD>JavaCast("String", 1999)</TD><TD>#JavaCast("String", 1999)#</TD></TR>
</TABLE>
</CFOUTPUT>
<CFTRY>
  <CFSET Vec = CreateObject("JAVA", "java.util.Vector")>
<CFCATCH TYPE="Object">
  <CFOUTPUT><P>Creating the Java object to pass them to: <I>#CFCATCH.Message#</I></CFOUTPUT>
</CFCATCH>
</CFTRY>
